Jamaica was an English, later British, colony in the Caribbean from 1655 to 1962. The map shows it in 1715.

An English fleet sent by Oliver Cromwell took the island from Spain in 1655. Its harbour town, Port Royal, became a base for buccaneers who raided Spanish America, led most famously by Henry Morgan. An earthquake sank much of Port Royal into the sea in 1692.

By 1715 Jamaica was turning into the largest British sugar island, and enslaved Africans from the Atlantic slave trade soon made up the great majority of its people. Many escaped to the mountains, and the Maroons fought Britain until treaties in 1739 recognised their freedom. Tacky's Revolt of 1760 was one of the largest slave revolts in the British Caribbean.

Britain freed the enslaved under the Slavery Abolition Act of 1833. Jamaica became independent in 1962. See also Jamaica on the map.
sum: Jamaica was an English, later British, colony in the Caribbean from 1655 to 1962. The map shows it in 1715.
